result.title: RubricOpt: Self-Revision of Semantic Rubrics for Preference Optimization
result.summary: A model's failures can reveal gaps in the behavioral criteria guiding its training. We introduce RubricOpt, a framework that lets a policy revise these criteria within preference optimization. The policy diagnoses its own rubric-free outputs, retains requirements already covered by the rubric, and edits clauses that leave recurring failures unaddressed. A shared semantic representation connects task demands, preference-data contrasts, and rubric clauses, while a deterministic gate checks evidence references and fixed semantic anchors. The rubric then guides Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) during training, with preference pairs, labels, and the objective held fixed, and is removed at evaluation. Our analysis relates the local effect on rubric-free success to semantic alignment and a residual beyond the measured factors. Experiments on capability and open-ended generation benchmarks show that rubric conditioning can improve outcomes over ordinary DPO, with gains and regressions varying across models and datasets. A matched continuation isolates the contribution of revision from additional training and finds mixed incremental effects for the tested edit, whose feedback overlaps the evaluation set. RubricOpt thus brings the behavioral specification itself into the policy's feedback loop.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RubricOpt：让策略在偏好优化中诊断自身无 rubric 时的输出，保留已被覆盖的要求并修订对反复失败无效的语义条款，用共享语义表示连接任务需求、偏好数据对比与条款，并以确定性门控核查证据引用，最后用 rubric 条件化 DPO 训练、评测时移除。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「自诊断—证据门控修订—在固定偏好数据上训练」的反馈闭环，可能为 LVR 的轨迹监督与贡献分配提供训练期线索；但该工作面向文本偏好对齐，是否可迁移到多模态推理状态需核查。
